test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 15 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Lactose intolerance is:

options.text: Characterised by adverse reactions to gluten
a condition in which the small intestines are unable to break down the sugars found in dairy products
a condition where small intestines are unable to break down gluten
a condition where fructose isn't efficiently absorbed into the blood

solution:
The correct answer is __**a condition in which the small intestines are unable to break down the sugars found in dairy products**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lactose intolerance** is a condition where the small intestines cannot effectively break down lactose, the sugar found in dairy products.
 
• This occurs due to a deficiency of lactase, the enzyme responsible for digesting lactose.
 
• Symptoms of lactose intolerance include bloating, diarrhea, and abdominal pain after consuming dairy products.
 
• It is different from a milk allergy, which involves the immune system reacting to proteins in milk.
 
• Management of lactose intolerance often involves dietary adjustments, such as reducing or eliminating dairy intake or using lactose-free products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lactase persistence** is the continued activity of the lactase enzyme into adulthood, which is genetically determined and varies among populations.
 
• Populations with historically high dairy consumption, such as those in Northern Europe, have higher rates of lactase persistence.
 
• **Non-dairy calcium sources** include leafy green vegetables, fortified plant-based milks, and supplements.
 
• Some individuals with lactose intolerance can tolerate small amounts of dairy or certain dairy products like hard cheeses and yogurt.
 
• Consulting with a healthcare provider or a dietitian can help in managing lactose intolerance effectively.
